correctness.rationale: The exact Parseval fiber identity yields all squared frame bounds. A known generalized Vandermonde factorization maps determinant to F(X,Y) on a full compact square. Derivative identities enumerate all nonzero interior critical values D± and boundary values; the larger D+ is attained. Every equality branch is the same rotated/permuted symmetric three-node set. The unit-length sum argument rules out tightness. Symbolic identities and direct numerical matrix comparison were reproduced by checker.py, whose finite tests are only auxiliary.

value.rationale: This solves the sharp determinant/volume-optimal choice of three lattice frequency shifts for the natural first sparse three-cell non-orthogonal multittile. General multittile Riesz theory does not choose these shifts. The non-equilateral optimum, exact algebraic sharp constant, and rigid equality geometry provide a reproducible frequency design fact without asserting a stronger downstream theorem.
